quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your vehicle does not have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal down.
Pump the brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. Your car will stop faster and you can still steer.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheels straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels sharply to the left, away from the curb. If your brakes fail, your vehicle will roll toward the curb instead of into traffic.

questions.question: What should a driver do when approaching an uncontrolled intersection?

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop, look both ways, and then go.
Yield to all other drivers.
Be ready to yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no stop sign or traffic light, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be prepared to yield by taking your foot off the gas, covering the brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used as a traffic signal.
It means the same as a red traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction the arrow shows.
Traffic in that direction must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same as a red traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a circular red traffic light. Traffic in that lane must stop and cannot turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.question: When parallel parking, how far from the curb should you be?

options.text: 10 inches
12 inches
18 inches
24 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 inches
questions.explanation: When parallel parking, your wheels should be parallel to the curb and within 12 inches of it. Park only where you will not block traffic and where drivers can see your vehicle from both directions.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow arrow traffic signal?

options.text: Merge into the lane in the direction the arrow shows.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
You have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic will stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow allows left turns in that direction. However, oncoming traffic has a green light, so you must yield to them and to pedestrians.

questions.question: When can you cross double solid yellow lines?

options.text: To pass a slow truck.
To turn into a driveway.
To pass another car.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: To turn into a driveway.
questions.explanation: Double solid lines mean no passing or lane changes. You can only cross them to turn left into or out of a driveway, to enter or exit a highway, or to make a legal U-turn.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop, look for traffic, then go if it is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and drive carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells drivers to slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system cause?

options.text: Use too much oil.
Require a tune-up sooner than normal.
Make you drowsy while driving.
Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you drowsy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases, reduces noise, and cools hot gases from the engine. Fumes from a leaky exhaust can cause drowsiness while driving and can be deadly.

questions.question: What must you do to pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road?

options.text: Do not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the lane for oncoming traffic. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are dangerous.
The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
The suggested speed to drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the highest or lowest legal speed you can drive on a road when conditions are ideal. You can drive slower than the posted speed, but you cannot drive faster. You must drive slower in school zones and work zones. If road construction or bad weather makes the posted speed unsafe, drive slower than the limit.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, what should you do with your wheels?

options.text: Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.
Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
Keep your front wheels straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parked facing uphill, turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb. This keeps your vehicle from rolling into traffic. If there is no curb, turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green arrow on a traffic light?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting other vehicles and pedestrians in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane for the turn. Let any vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection pass first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines are doubled in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns drivers that the road ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: An approaching driver does not dim their bright headlights. Where should you look?

options.text: At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.
Toward the right side of the road.
Toward the left side of the road.
Straight down the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road if an approaching driver does not dim their bright headlights. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road well enough to stay on course until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so other drivers let you through.
Drive around the back of a car that blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If another car hits you from behind, straight wheels keep you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: Your vehicle's stopping distance increases when stopping on:

options.text: A wet or icy road.
Paved highways.
During night driving.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A wet or icy road.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance increases on wet or icy roads. It also increases on roads covered with loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: You come to a flashing red light. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for the light to turn solid green.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. Then proceed when the road is clear.

questions.question: You want to back out of your driveway and see children playing nearby. What should you do first?

options.text: Rev your engine to warn the children you are moving.
Honk your horn so the children hear you.
Walk to the back of your car to check the way is clear.
Tell the children to leave the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk to the back of your car to check the way is clear.
questions.explanation: Look through your back window for pedestrians and obstacles when you back up. Do not rely only on your mirrors, especially around children. Always get out and check behind your vehicle before backing out of a driveway.

questions.question: Under good weather and traffic conditions, what is the minimum distance you should stay behind another vehicle?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep more distance between your vehicle and others to have more time to react. Keep a minimum following distance of three seconds under normal weather and traffic conditions. Increase your distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Road construction ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead curves right and then left. Slow down to safely navigate these curves.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not have enough time to stop.

questions.question: How far before turning should you signal?

options.text: 100 feet
50 feet
20 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. Use your arm signal or turn signal to let other drivers know your plans. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn.
Turn right at the intersection.
Parking area ahead.
A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: A crossroad is ahead. Watch for traffic.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a crossroad is ahead.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle yet. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
Pull to the curb and check if the vehicle is on your street.
Slow down but do not stop until you see it.
Speed up and turn at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the curb and check if the vehicle is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren but do not know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until you are sure it is not heading toward you.
